title: Christmas 2019: Make Every Day Count
keywords: Association of Retired Supreme Court Justices
Charlie Brown Snoopy we only die once
Moonlight Terrace Jai Alai Manila Hotel
primary_topics: Annual Christmas talk delivered to the Association of Retired Supreme Court Justices, November 27, 2019, at the request of CJ Hilario G. Davide Jr. as president
The 'Make Every Day Count' philosophy: retirees in their 70s, 80s and beyond have been granted bonus days by God; 'We only die once. We live every day' (Snoopy to Charlie Brown)
Nostalgic reminiscence of judicial and social life in earlier decades -- bus fares, taxi fares, exchange rates, dating spots, favorite singers -- as a celebration of life lived
Technology outlook for the next generation: 5G, AI, IoT, crypto currencies, stem cell technology, telomere lengthening, and the possibility of disease-optional death by 2045
sub_topics: CJP's humorous opening: CJ Davide 'must be a glutton for punishment' for asking him to deliver a homily every year; 'here's his penance -- totaling 50 pages. But because of the Christmas season, I will read only 49 pages!'

Welcome to new retirees: newly-retired CJ Luke (Peralta? -- the full CJ is referred to as 'CJ Dado Peralta who is here with us today') and Senior Justice Tony -- thanked for implementing retirement benefits equal to incumbent emoluments

Retirement benefits structure: retirees receive benefits equal to incumbents' emoluments; when incumbents get a raise, retirees do too; survivorship clause: surviving spouses receive the full benefits during their lifetime -- but Justice Minita Chico-Nazario clarified that survivorship applies only to the original spouse, not future partners

The Charlie Brown / Snoopy cartoon joke: Charlie Brown: 'We only live once.' Snoopy: 'Wrong! We only die once. We live every day.' -- 'Let us make each day count. Smile, laugh, sing, dance, travel and enjoy life till we reach 100 and beyond'

Bar exam memories: rivalry among UP, Ateneo, San Carlos, and the University Belt schools (UST, San Beda, MLQ, UE, FEU); bus fare 10-15 centavos (Halili Transit, JD Transit); taxi 10 centavos flag down + 5 centavos per half-kilometer; 2-4 pesos = 1 US dollar = 360 Japanese yen; dating at Moonlight Terrace, Jai Alai Sky Room, Winter Garden of Manila Hotel
Favorite singers of that era: Sylvia La Torre, Ruben Tagalog, Diomedes Maturan, Pilita Corrales; newest sensation: Moira de la Torre
Technology changes: from two-year telephone waits (party lines) to instant hand-carried phones; Skype, Facetime, Viber, WhatsApp, Telegram for free international calls; snap-and-share on smart phones
5G ripple effects: buy anything from talipapas via smart phones; CCTV monitoring of bedrooms and kitchens from abroad
AI, crypto, IoT beyond 5G -- within five years
Stem cell revolution: grandchildren may live 150 years; spare hearts, limbs, brains grown and traded in; Chernobyl/Fukushima analysis by Bill Gates; nuclear energy safe, cheap and 24/7 potential
Telomere shortening as the cause of ageing; laboratory experiments showing arrest and even lengthening of telomeres; Google and Microsoft veering to these sciences
Death 'optional' by 2045: advance medical knowledge eliminating dead cells, repairing damaged cells, regenerating new ones
Einstein brain / bar flunker joke: brains auctioned at Sotheby's; Einstein's at $1,000 (overused), Filipino bar flunker Alberto Estan's at $100,000 (almost new and underused)

stances.claim: Long-lived retirees -- those who have exceeded the Philippine average longevity of ~70 years -- are living on 'bonus days, months, years and even decades' granted by God. The proper response is not passive waiting but active, joyful living: 'Smile, laugh, sing, dance, travel and enjoy life till we reach 100 and beyond.' Snoopy's inversion ('we only die once; we live every day') is the governing philosophy.
stances.rhetorical_move: bonus-days theology: the surplus years beyond average longevity reframed as a divine gift requiring deliberate enjoyment
stances.confidence: asserted as personal credo for the association of retired justices

stances.claim: By 2045, death from disease may be 'optional' due to stem cell technology, telomere lengthening, and the conquest of cancer, heart failure, diabetes and physical disabilities. This is not science fiction but a trajectory already underway in major tech companies like Google and Microsoft.
stances.rhetorical_move: futures-projection argument: the technology trajectory as a reason for the next generation's optimism about longevity
stances.confidence: asserted as informed speculation with named companies

stances.claim: Retirement is not the end of productive work but merely a 'change of tires to embark on a new journey.' CJP himself proves it: 13 years after retiring from the SC, he is still an active director, trustee, columnist, and FLP chairman.

notable_anecdotes: The survivorship clause aside: CJP was kidding the widows that their financial benefits would 'attract suitors and future spouses.' Justice Minita Chico-Nazario firmly clarified: 'the survivorship clause applies only to the original spouse, not to future husbands or future wives or future lovers.'

Charlie Brown and Snoopy: Charlie Brown gazes at night stars and says 'We only live once.' Snoopy replies: 'Wrong! We only die once. We live every day.' CJP: 'Let us make each day count. Smile, laugh, sing, dance, travel and enjoy life till we reach 100 and beyond.'

Bar exam era nostalgia: bus fare 10-15 centavos (Halili Transit, JD Transit); taxi 10 centavos flag down + 5 centavos per half-kilometer; 2-4 pesos = 1 US dollar = 360 Japanese yen; dating at the Moonlight Terrace, the Jai Alai Sky Room, or the Winter Garden of the Manila Hotel; favorite singers Sylvia La Torre, Ruben Tagalog, Diomedes Maturan, Pilita Corrales (vs. newest sensation Moira de la Torre).

The Einstein brain / bar flunker joke: brains auctioned at Sotheby's -- Einstein's at $1,000, Filipino Alberto Estan (failed bar thrice) at $100,000. Why? 'Einstein's brain is already overused while the bar flunker's brain is almost new and underused.' CJP closes: 'May we all have underused brains so our heirs may inherit them and fill them up with wit and wisdom we missed in our own carefree lives listening to irreverent speeches and corny jokes like mine.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 27, 2019 at the annual Christmas gathering of the Association of Retired Supreme Court Justices -- at the request of CJ Hilario Davide Jr. who serves as the association's president and who 'must be a glutton for punishment' for asking CJP to deliver a homily every year ('here's his penance -- totaling 50 pages; but because of the Christmas season, I will read only 49!') -- this speech opens by welcoming newly-retired CJ Luke and Senior Justice Tony and thanking them for establishing retirement benefits equal to incumbents' emoluments with a survivorship clause, before Justice Minita Chico-Nazario firmly clarified that survivorship applies only to the original spouse, not future partners. The governing philosophy is 'Make Every Day Count': retirees have exceeded the Philippine average longevity of ~70 years and are living on 'bonus days, months, years and even decades' granted by God; a Viber cartoon of Charlie Brown ('We only live once') and Snoopy ('Wrong! We only die once. We live every day') provides the epigram. CJP leads a nostalgic tour of the bar exam era: bus fares of 10-15 centavos (Halili Transit, JD Transit), taxis at 10 centavos flag-down, 2-4 pesos to a US dollar, 360 yen to a dollar, dates at the Moonlight Terrace and Winter Garden of the Manila Hotel, favorite singers Sylvia La Torre, Ruben Tagalog, Diomedes Maturan, Pilita Corrales -- versus today's newest sensation Moira de la Torre. He then pivots to the technology future: 5G ripple effects, AI, crypto and IoT within five years; beyond those, stem cell technology enabling grandchildren to grow spare hearts, limbs and brains; telomere lengthening experiments; Bill Gates' nuclear energy safety research; and the prediction by genetic engineers that death from disease will be 'optional' by 2045. He closes with his Einstein/bar-flunker joke: brains auctioned at Sotheby's -- Einstein's at $1,000 (overused) vs. Filipino Alberto Estan's at $100,000 (almost new and underused). 'May we all have underused brains so our heirs may inherit them and fill them up with wit and wisdom we missed in our own carefree lives.'
